page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn1.7xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture using KVM virtualization. The instance features an Intel Xeon 8163 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz, delivering 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. It includes 64.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a 1:2 compute-optimized ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware features encompass instruction set extensions such as AVX, AVX-512F, FMA, BMI2, and hardware AES acceleration, backed by 33 MB of L3 cache. The instance provision does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPUs, and it provides a baseline network throughput of 6 Gbps.

Benchmark measurements indicate a profile geared toward parallel computation rather than single-threaded speed. In Geekbench tests, single-core processing registered a weak score of 960.0, while multi-core operations scaled to an average 8426.0. Similarly, stress-ng showed lower single-core throughput (1109.99) alongside solid multi-core performance (23557.71). Memory throughput demonstrates 74.54 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads and 34.35 GB/sec for uncached writes, while the overall PassMark memory score ranked in the bottom quartile at 1809.96. Workloads dependent on single-threaded execution, such as single-stream gzip compression, reflect reduced speeds.

The primary architectural tradeoff for the ecs.sn1.7xlarge centers on balancing older-generation single-core execution speeds against multi-core horizontal scalability. With 32 dedicated vCPUs, the instance delivers dependable multi-threaded performance in compilation (Geekbench clang score of 18724.0), ray tracing (19799.0), and Redis operations (23.27 million ops/sec). Because it provides dedicated execution units with a 1:2 memory configuration, it provides a stable environment for scalable parallel workloads, multi-threaded batch processes, static web serving clusters, and distributed build systems.
